title: Self-heating ring bistability
description: Thermo-optic bistability of a self-heating microring (models/optical_field/ring_selfheat.va): a 50 uW CW laser drives a high-Q ring whose absorbed circulating power heats it, and silicon's dn/dT > 0 red-shifts the resonance — a nonlinear feedback loop. A PWL source (LAM) ramps the laser wavelength across the cold resonance and back in one transient. The through-port traces a HYSTERESIS loop: sweeping to the red the heated resonance locks to the laser (extended, triangular thermal-locking dip) then snaps back; sweeping back to the blue the ring stays cold until the cold resonance (sharp Lorentzian dip). Forward and backward switch at different wavelengths — the classic fingerprint of optical thermal bistability. The pinned physics study is examples/ring_selfheat.py.

notes.title: Self-heating ring — thermo-optic bistability
lines: A 50 uW CW laser (LAS) drives the all-pass ring RG
(ring_selfheat). The fraction heat_frac of the intrinsic
loss that is absorbed heats a one-pole thermal reservoir
red-shifts the resonance, closing a feedback loop.
RG reads the laser wavelength from its electrical node
`lam` (V(lam) = wavelength in nm). The PWL source LAM
(>> tau_th, so quasi-static). Probe thru = through-port
power; probe lam = the wavelength ramp (in 'volts' = nm).
Forward (blue->red, 0-40 us) the hot resonance locks to
the laser: an extended triangular dip, dragged red, that
snaps back. Backward (red->blue, 40-80 us) the ring is
cold: through ~ 1 until the sharp cold-cavity dip near
1310.000 nm. The two directions dip at different times =
hysteresis. Raise LAS.power to 100e-6 to widen the loop;
